purpose: build the user-facing part of the application so it is correct, fast, accessible and maintainable, using the agreed designs and API contracts
entry_criteria: Approved designs and an API contract exist
A design system or component library is in place
The browser and device support policy is known
procedure: Build from the design system components, and extend them rather than writing page-specific copies; use semantic HTML and correct roles so accessibility starts from structure.
Handle all states: loading, empty, error and success, plus validation messages and disabled states, against the real API contract using mocks until the backend exists.
Manage state deliberately: keep server data in a data-fetching layer with caching, local state local, and avoid duplicating the same data in several stores.
Meet performance budgets: control bundle size with code splitting, optimize images, defer non-critical scripts and measure Core Web Vitals.
Protect against common web risks: escape output, avoid unsafe HTML insertion, use content security policy and keep tokens out of local storage where the design allows.
Test with unit and component tests, accessibility checks and a few end-to-end journeys, and run them in CI.
deliverables: components and pages built from the design system
acceptance_criteria: Semantic HTML and keyboard use are verified
Performance budgets are measured and met
Untrusted data is never inserted as HTML

validation.command: npx --no-install vitest run && npx --no-install playwright test --grep @a11y   # example; use the project's tools

failure_modes.response: Add a size budget in CI
Escape and add a content security policy

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A product list page uses the design system table, shows skeleton, empty and error states, fetches through a cached data layer, and a CI budget fails the build if the main bundle grows by more than 10 percent.
